This application, under section 528 of the BNSS, has been filed for quashment of order dated 02/09/2024 passed by I Additional Sessions Judge, Gohad, District Bhind in Cr.R. No. 27/2023 and order dated 16/5/2023 passed by JMFC Gohad, District Bhind.

sentences.text: 2. The facts necessary for disposal of the present application are that the complainant/respondent no.1 filed an application under section 156(3) of the Cr.P.C. complaining commission of offences under sections 420, 467, 468, 471 and 120B of the IPC on the ground that he is Pujari of Narsingh Mandir, Ward No.10, Gohad, District Bhind.
The Manager of the temple is Collector.
The Collector is also the Manager of Shri Mahavir Mandir.
The complainant was disciple of Shri Dayaramdas Guru Bhagwandas, who was Mahant of both the temples.
Shri Dayaramdasji expired on 23/03/2020.
The NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-GWL:19600 2 MCRC-47294-2024 complainant is looking after the maintenance, security and prayer in the temple since the lifetime of Dayaramdasji.
Dayaramdasji had also executed a registered power of attorney in favour of complainant in the year 2007.
SDO Gohad, District Bhind also appointed him as Pujari by order dated 30/11/2022 passed in Case No. 144/21-22/B-121.
It was alleged that after the death of Dayaramdasji, a forged Will has been prepared with forged signatures of Mahant Shri Dayaramdasji.

It is further alleged that on the basis of forged Will, the accused persons moved an application for mutation of their names as well as for appointment of Pujari before Tahsildar,

sentences.text: The complainant obtained a report from forensic expert, who has opined that the signatures on the Will are different from that of Shri Dayaramdasji.
Accordingly, a complaint was made to Superintendent of Police, Bhind.
However, no action was taken.
The accused persons are creating all sorts of hurdle in maintenance of temple.
Even the CCTV cameras installed in the premises of temple were damaged and report in that regard was also lodged on 18/11/2021, 25/01/2022 and 4/11/2022.
Complainant was beaten and report in that regard was also made on 3/1/2022, 25/2/2022 and 29/5/2022, but no action was taken and accordingly the complaint was filed.
3. The trial Magistrate, by order dated 16/5/2023, directed the Police to register the offences.
Being aggrieved by the said order, applicants preferred a revision, which has been dismissed.
4. It is submitted by counsel for the applicants that Prem Kishore Katare was minor and he has performed the last rites of Shri Dayaramdasji.
Therefore, it is clear that the allegation of preparing forged Will is incorrect.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-GWL:19600 3 MCRC-47294-2024
It is further submitted that there is no allegation against applicant no.5 Pop Singh.
It is further submitted that there is no allegation against applicant Ram Sagar.

5. Heard, learned counsel for the applicants.
6.
So far as Pop Singh is concerned, he is the witness of Will.
If the Will is found to be forged, then Pop Singh will be equally responsible.
Accordingly, it is clear that the submission made by learned counsel for the applicants that there is no allegation against Pop Singh is misconceived and it is,
accordingly
, rejected.

So far as applicant Prem Kishore Katare is concerned, even if it is assumed that he had performed the last rites of Shri Dayaramdasji, that by itself would not be sufficient to hold that the Will was a genuine one.
So far as Ram Sagar is concerned, there is specific allegation against Ram Sagar with regard to preparation of forged Will.
Furthermore, an order under section 156(3) of Cr.P.C. does not mean that the applicants have been held guilty.
Police has jurisdiction to investigate the matter and to come to a conclusion and thereafter to file a final report (closure report or charge-sheet).

If closure report is filed, the same shall be decided by the Magistrate after giving an opportunity of hearing to the complainant and if charge-sheet is filed, the applicants shall have the right to face the trial or challenge the charge-sheet.

However, this Court cannot stop the investigation in mid-way thereby restraining the police Authorities from collecting evidence without adjudicating the correctness of allegations made in the complaint.

7. Thus, this Court is of the considered opinion that neither the trial NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2024:MPHC-GWL:19600 4 MCRC-47294-2024 Magistrate nor the Revisional Court committed any mistake by passing an order under section 156(3) of the Cr.P.C. and by dismissing the revision arising out of the said order.
Accordingly, the orders dated 16/05/2023 and 02/09/2024 are affirmed.
